findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical meet-in-the-middle solution: it counts every nums1/nums2 pair sum with multiplicity, scans every nums3/nums4 pair, and adds the complementary frequency. It is concise, conventional, asymptotically appropriate, and expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 454 and its four-array Python contract. The manifest's O(n^2) expected time and O(n^2) space match the two pair products and the possible number of distinct first-half sums; the modular Reference now states all equal-length and value bounds.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064926156. Its Counter generator, variable roles, nested second-half loops, negated complement lookup with a zero default, and accumulated return value are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only annotations and the LeetCode wrapper differ.

The all-zero widths 7, 21, and 49 span 7x and force both quadratic pair passes while retaining the closed-form n^4 result. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.99x the reference runtime. A correct three-loop-plus-frequency-table control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 20.06x.

The Approach exactly matches the protected target: it derives the two-half decomposition, explains why multiplicity rather than membership is required, proves each index tuple is counted once, and states the expected hash-table time and worst-case distinct-sum space. Its alternatives and duplicate-value traps are specific and accurate.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the independent index condition, both exact source examples, both qualifying tuples and their full arithmetic in the first explanation, and all six constraints. The unsupported legacy third example was removed from the source sequence.
